fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. "The king was enraged, and he sent his troops to destroy those murderers and burn their city." (Matthew 22:7) Troops fills the first blank, and city fills the second. This part is heavy, because the servants were killed in the verse before. The king's anger is the response to that.

Gifts would be a nice gesture, but nobody in the parable sends any. The text says they "…paid no attention and went away, one to his field, another to his business." (Matthew 22:5) They turned away and went about their day. Nothing like a gift shows up anywhere in the story.

The temple is where Jesus is teaching (Matthew 21:23), so it's a fair guess. But the parable never mentions a temple. The king says, "Go therefore to the crossroads and invite to the banquet as many as you can find." (Matthew 22:9) The servants are sent to the crossroads.

The parable never mentions a palace, baker. The king says, "Go therefore to the crossroads and invite to the banquet as many as you can find." (Matthew 22:9) That's where the servants are sent. The place the text names for the banquet is the "wedding hall." (Matthew 22:10)

Close, baker, but the king says nothing about important people. He tells the servants, "…invite to the banquet as many as you can find." (Matthew 22:9) The text gives no list of titles. The invitation just goes wide.

Only the good? That would be a very tidy guest list, baker. But the text says the servants gathered "…everyone they could find, both evil and good…" (Matthew 22:10) Both kinds are in that hall. The word is everyone.

Yes, baker! Jesus closes with "For many are called, but few are chosen." (Matthew 22:14) Many, then few. Those two numbers are not twins. It's a short line, and I'd chew on it slowly, like a cookie fresh out of the oven.
